objective_for_doctor: A 79-year-old F patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: laryngospasm.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I’ve been having laryngospasm, like I suddenly can’t breathe for a very short time and I’ve felt like I was suffocating, with inability to breathe or speak. I’m also having shortness of breath or difficulty breathing in a significant way.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—when these episodes happen, are you awake and fully conscious, and how long do the spells last (seconds vs minutes)?  
Doctor: Also, do you notice any triggers like eating, reflux/heartburn, recent anesthesia/dental work, choking/gagging, cold air, or strong emotions?

I’m awake and fully conscious, and the spells last a very short time. I don’t know about any specific triggers like eating, reflux/heartburn, recent anesthesia/dental work, choking/gagging, cold air, or strong emotions.

Doctor: Are you able to inhale normally right after the episode ends, and do you have stridor (a high-pitched sound) or cough/wheezing afterward?  
Doctor: Also, do you have any history of GERD/reflux, asthma/COPD, thyroid disease, or neurological problems, and have you had similar episodes with swallowing or choking?

I’m awake and fully conscious, and the spells last a very short time. I don’t know about any specific triggers like eating, reflux/heartburn, recent anesthesia/dental work, choking/gagging, cold air, or strong emotions.

Doctor: During the episodes do you make a high‑pitched sound when trying to breathe (stridor) and does it resolve completely afterward, and do you ever get hoarseness, a feeling of something stuck in the throat, or swelling?  
Doctor: Also, any recent upper respiratory infection, new medications (especially ACE inhibitors), or visible throat mass/ongoing dysphagia?

I don’t know about any triggers like eating, reflux/heartburn, recent anesthesia/dental work, choking/gagging, cold air, or strong emotions. Doctor: I need a couple specifics: do you get these episodes mainly at night or when lying down, and have you noticed heartburn/regurgitation, chronic throat clearing, or sour taste?  
Doctor: Also, have you had any difficulty swallowing solids/liquids, unintentional weight loss, or progressive voice changes?

I don’t know about whether the episodes are mainly at night or when lying down. I don’t know about heartburn/regurgitation, chronic throat clearing, or sour taste. I also don’t know about any difficulty swallowing solids/liquids, unintentional weight loss, or progressive voice changes.

Doctor: If you can, also tell me whether you have any history of seizures, panic attacks, or recent stroke/TIA symptoms (one-sided weakness, facial droop, sudden speech trouble), and whether you smoke or have known airway/throat disease.  
Doctor: Lastly, do you currently have any symptoms between episodes (hoarseness, persistent shortness of breath, wheeze), and have you ever been told you have sleep apnea or used CPAP?

Also, during your episodes are you able to catch your breath fully afterward (yes/no), and do you take any new meds—especially ACE inhibitors or opioids?
